title: Rigveda 10.122: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.122: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.122 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 109r-110r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.122.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 109r
translation.original_text:
1vasu̱ṁ na ci̱trama̍hasaṁ gṛṇīṣe vā̱maṁ śeva̱m ati̍thim adviṣe̱ṇyam | sa rā̍sate śu̱rudho̍ vi̱śvadhā̍yaso̱ 'gnir hotā̍ gṛ̱hapa̍tiḥ su̱vīrya̍m ||
2ju̱ṣā̱ṇo a̍gne̱ prati̍ harya me̱ vaco̱ viśvā̍ni vi̱dvān va̱yunā̍ni sukrato | ghṛta̍nirṇi̱g brahma̍ṇe gā̱tum era̍ya̱ tava̍ de̱vā a̍janaya̱nn anu̍ vra̱tam ||
3sa̱pta dhāmā̍ni pari̱yann ama̍rtyo̱ dāśa̍d dā̱śuṣe̍ su̱kṛte̍ māmahasva | su̱vīre̍ṇa ra̱yiṇā̍gne svā̱bhuvā̱ yas ta̱ āna̍ṭ sa̱midhā̱ taṁ ju̍ṣasva ||
translation.text:
1I PRAISE the God of wondrous might like Indra, the lovely pleasant Guest whom all must welcome. May Agni, Priest and Master of the household, give hero strength and all-sustaining riches.
2O Agni, graciously accept this song of mine, thou passing-wise who knowest every ordinance. Enwrapped in holy oil further the course of prayer: the Gods bestow according to thy holy law.
3Immortal, wandering round the seven stations, give, a liberal Giver, to the pious worshipper, Wealth, Agni, with brave sons and ready for his use: welcome the man who comes with fuel unto thee.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 109r (OPenn image 108, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.121.10 ‹-viśvā jātāni pari tā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 109v, begins in RV 10.122.4 ‹-purohitaṁ haviṣmanta īḻate sapta›. Verses 10.122.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.122.4-7 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 109v
translation.original_text:
4ya̱jñasya̍ ke̱tum pra̍tha̱mam pu̱rohi̍taṁ ha̱viṣma̍nta īḻate sa̱pta vā̱jina̍m | śṛ̱ṇvanta̍m a̱gniṁ ghṛ̱tapṛ̍ṣṭham u̱kṣaṇa̍m pṛ̱ṇanta̍ṁ de̱vam pṛ̍ṇa̱te su̱vīrya̍m ||
5tvaṁ dū̱taḥ pra̍tha̱mo vare̍ṇya̱ḥ sa hū̱yamā̍no a̱mṛtā̍ya matsva | tvām ma̍rjayan ma̱ruto̍ dā̱śuṣo̍ gṛ̱he tvāṁ stome̍bhi̱r bhṛga̍vo̱ vi ru̍rucuḥ ||
6iṣa̍ṁ du̱han su̱dughā̍ṁ vi̱śvadhā̍yasaṁ yajña̱priye̱ yaja̍mānāya sukrato | agne̍ ghṛ̱tasnu̱s trir ṛ̱tāni̱ dīdya̍d va̱rtir ya̱jñam pa̍ri̱yan su̍kratūyase ||
7tvām id a̱syā u̱ṣaso̱ vyu̍ṣṭiṣu dū̱taṁ kṛ̍ṇvā̱nā a̍yajanta̱ mānu̍ṣāḥ | tvāṁ de̱vā ma̍ha̱yāyyā̍ya vāvṛdhu̱r ājya̍m agne nimṛ̱janto̍ adhva̱re ||
translation.text:
4The seven who bring oblations worship thee, the Strong, the first, the Great Chief Priest, Ensign of sacrifice, The oil-anointed Bull, Agni who hears, who sends as God full hero strength to him who freely gives.
5First messenger art thou, meet for election: drink thou thy fill invited to the Anirta, The Maruts in the votary's house adorned thee; with lauds the Bhr̥igus gave thee light and glory.
6Milking the teeming Cow for all-sustaining food. O Wise One, for the worship-loving worshipper, Thou, Agni, dropping oil, thrice lighting works of Law, showest thy wisdom circling home and sacrifice.
7They who at flushing of this dawn appointed thee their messenger, these men have paid thee reverence. Gods strengthened thee for work that must be glorified, Agni, while they made butter pure for sacrifice.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.122.8 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 110r
translation.original_text: <sup>8</sup>ni tvā̱ vasi̍ṣṭhā ahvanta vā̱jina̍ṁ gṛ̱ṇanto̍ agne vi̱dathe̍ṣu ve̱dhasa̍ḥ | rā̱yas poṣa̱ṁ yaja̍māneṣu dhāraya yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>8</sup>Arrangers in our synods, Agni, while they sang Vasisistha s sons have called thee down, the Potent One. Maintain the growth of wealth with men who sacrifice. Ye Gods, preserve us with your blessings evermore.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 110r (OPenn image 109, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.122.8 ‹-ahvanta vājinaṁ gṛṇanto agne›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 110v, begins in RV 10.123.4 ‹hi gman›. Verse 10.122.8 ends on this page; 10.122.8 begins on fol. 109v.
